extracted.intended_audience: general readers and prospective contributors (writers/poets/essayists) interested in Strange Horizons and online speculative fiction magazines
extracted.subtask_description: Information about Strange Horizons as a publication venue — its editorial emphasis, genres it publishes, publication frequency, organizational model, and recognition; useful for writers considering submission or researching the magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on new, underrepresented, and global voices
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine publishes new material ... with an emphasis on "new, underrepresented, and global voices."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated editorial focus that signals preference for work by newer authors, writers from underrepresented backgrounds, and work representing global perspectives. This is an explicit selection priority mentioned in the magazine's profile on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres published
rubrics_metrics.description: Strange Horizons is an online speculative fiction magazine. It also features speculative poetry and non-fiction in every issue, including reviews, essays, interviews, and roundtables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts a range of speculative-genre content: fiction, poetry, and non-fiction (reviews, essays, interviews, roundtables). The phrasing indicates these genres are core to each issue and therefore represent the types of work a prospective contributor should submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency / regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: It publishes new material (fiction, articles, reviews, poetry, and/or art) 51 weeks of the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weekly/new-material cadence (with one week off per year) — implies a steady stream of publishing opportunities and expectations of timely editorial workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational model and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: It is registered with the IRS as 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. The magazine has a staff of approximately sixty volunteers, and is unusual among professional speculative fiction magazines in being funded entirely by donations, holding annual fund drives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-profit, largely volunteer-run, donation-funded model may affect editorial practices, payment structures, and submission handling; signals the magazine's institutional values and reliance on community support rather than commercial publishing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent inclusion of poetry and non-fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: It also features speculative poetry and non-fiction in every issue, including reviews, essays, interviews, and roundtables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike some venues that occasionally run non-fiction or poetry, Strange Horizons commits to including these elements in each issue — important for poets and essayists evaluating fit and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional recognition and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine and its editors have been nominated for and won numerous awards (e.g., finalist for the Hugo Award for Best Website in 2002 and 2005; won the Hugo Award for Best Semiprozine in 2024; editors have won/been nominated for World Fantasy and British Fantasy awards; stories published have been nominated for Hugo and Nebula awards and have won the Theodore Sturgeon Award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track record of nominations and awards indicates prestige and visibility for contributors; specific examples on the page demonstrate the magazine's standing in the field and the potential reach/recognition work published there can achieve.
